name: Grain Weevil
description: A major storage pest of cereal grains, particularly maize and rice. Adult weevils bore into grains to lay eggs, and larvae develop inside kernels, causing weight loss, reduced germination, and complete grain destruction in severe infestations.
symptoms: Small round holes in grain kernels
Fine grain dust at bottom of storage containers
Adult weevils visible crawling on grain surface
Heating and moisture buildup in stored grain
Complete grain hollowing in severe infestation
treatments: Mix grain with food-grade diatomaceous earth at storage
Apply neem leaf powder or neem oil to stored grain
Use hermetic storage bags (GrainPro, Purdue Improved Crop Storage bags)
Apply phosphine fumigation for severe infestations in sealed storage
Freeze infested grain at -18°C for 48 hours
prevention: Dry grain thoroughly (<13% moisture) before storage
Clean storage containers thoroughly before filling
Store in airtight or hermetic containers
Inspect stored grain regularly for early detection
Treat grain with botanical protectants (neem, chili pepper)
Store off the ground on pallets away from walls
